A cone of height 24 cm and base radius 10 cm is cut parallel to its base at half its height. Find the total surface area of the frustum formed.
qs.e: Frustum R = 10, r = 5, slant 13; 195π + 100π + 25π = 320π. (195π is only the curved part.)

qs.e: (2/3)(216) = 144; one cone = ⅓(9)(4) = 12; 144 ÷ 12 = 12. (24 treats the hemisphere as (4/3)πr³.)

Water flows at 5 km/h through a pipe of diameter 14 cm into a rectangular tank 50 m long and 44 m wide. Time for the water level to rise by 7 cm: (π = 22/7)
A sphere of diameter 6 cm is dropped into a cylindrical vessel of radius 6 cm partly filled with water. If it is completely submerged, the water level rises by:
qs.e: (4/3)π(27) = π(36)h ⇒ h = 1. (8 uses 6 as the sphere's radius; 0.25 uses 12 as the vessel's radius.)

qs.q: A cylindrical vessel of radius 30 cm contains water. A spherical iron ball dropped into it raises the water level by 5 cm. The radius of the ball is:
Marbles of diameter 1.4 cm are dropped into a cylindrical beaker of diameter 7 cm containing water. How many marbles will raise the water level by 5.6 cm?
In a shower, 5 cm of rain falls. The volume of water that falls on 1.5 hectares of ground is:
2 cm of rain falls on a flat roof 22 m × 20 m and all of it is collected in a cylindrical tank of diameter 2 m. The water level in the tank rises by: (π = 22/7)
qs.e: 8.8 m³ ÷ (22/7 × 1²) = 2.8 m. (0.7 uses 2 m as the radius.)

qs.q: A canal 6 m wide and 1.5 m deep carries water at 10 km/h. How much area can it irrigate in 30 minutes if 8 cm of standing water is needed?
Water flows at 6 m/s through a pipe of internal diameter 2 cm into a cylindrical tank of radius 40 cm and height 3 m. Time to fill the tank:
qs.e: Flow = π(1²)(600) = 600π cm³/s; tank = π(1600)(300) = 480000π ⇒ 800 s. (200 s uses 2 cm as radius.)

qs.q: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of radius 7 cm. How many litres flow out in one minute? (π = 22/7)
A cube of edge 6 cm is completely immersed in a cuboidal tank whose base is 20 cm × 15 cm. The rise in water level is:
Water from a full cylindrical vessel of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is poured into an empty cuboidal tank with base 22 cm × 10 cm. Height of water in the tank: (π = 22/7)

Water flows at 9 km/h through a rectangular channel 0.5 m × 0.4 m into a tank 40 m × 30 m. Time for the level to rise by 3 m:
A toy is in the form of a cone mounted on a hemisphere. The radius of the hemisphere and that of the cone is 36 cm and height of the cone is 105 cm. The total surface area of the toy is:
A hemispherical depression of diameter 4 cm is cut out from each face of a cubical block of side 10 cm. Find the surface area of the remaining solid. (π = 22/7)
qs.e: Each face nets +πr² = 4π; 600 + 24 × 22/7 = 675 3/7. SSC CGL 2021 (18 Apr 2022 S1).

qs.q: A toy is a cone mounted on a hemisphere of common radius 7 cm. The total height of the toy is 31 cm. Its total surface area is: (π = 22/7)
qs.e: Cone h = 31 − 7 = 24, l = 25; πr(l + 2r) = 22 × 39 = 858. (1012 adds the joining circle; 836 uses h for l; 1166 adds both full TSAs.)

qs.q: A solid toy is a hemisphere surmounted by a cone. The cone has height 4 cm and base diameter 8 cm. The volume of the toy is:
qs.e: r = 4: cone 64π/3 + hemisphere 128π/3 = 192π/3 = 64π. (320π/3 uses a full sphere.)

qs.q: A solid is a cylinder of radius 7 cm and length 20 cm with a hemisphere fixed at each end. Its total surface area is: (π = 22/7)
qs.e: 2πr(h + 2r) = 44 × 34 = 1496. (1804 adds the two joining circles; 1188 has one hemisphere; 880 is the cylinder only.)

qs.q: A capsule has a cylindrical middle and hemispherical ends. Its total length is 16 cm and its radius is 3 cm. Its volume is:
qs.e: Cylinder part = 16 − 6 = 10: 90π + (4/3)π(27) = 90π + 36π = 126π. (180π uses 16 as the cylinder length.)

qs.q: A tent is a cylinder of radius 14 m and height 3 m surmounted by a cone of the same radius and height 10.5 m. Canvas needed (no floor): (π = 22/7)
From a solid cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 8 cm, a cone of the same radius and height is hollowed out. The total surface area of the remaining solid is:
qs.e: l = 10; 2πrh + πr² + πrl = 96π + 36π + 60π = 192π. (228π keeps both end circles; 168π is the plain cylinder.)

qs.q: A solid is a cone on a hemisphere of the same radius r, and the cone's height equals r. The ratio of the volume of the cone part to the hemisphere part is:
A cone, a hemisphere and a cylinder stand on equal bases and have the same height. The ratio of their volumes is:
qs.e: Height = r (the hemisphere's height): ⅓πr³ : ⅔πr³ : πr³ = 1 : 2 : 3.

qs.q: An ice-cream cone of radius 3 cm and height 9 cm is filled and topped with a hemisphere of ice cream of the same radius. The total volume of ice cream is:
qs.e: ⅓π(9)(9) + ⅔π(27) = 27π + 18π = 45π. (63π uses a full sphere; 99π forgets ⅓.)

qs.q: From a solid cylinder of height 10 cm and radius 3.5 cm, a hemisphere of radius 3.5 cm is scooped out of each end. The total surface area of the article is: (π = 22/7)
qs.e: 2πrh + 2 × 2πr² = 220 + 154 = 374. (297 counts flat circles instead of bowls; 451 adds both.)

qs.q: A hemisphere of the largest possible size is placed on top of a cube of edge 7 cm. The total surface area of the solid is: (π = 22/7)
qs.e: r = 3.5; 6a² − πr² + 2πr² = 294 + 38.5 = 332.5. (371 forgets to remove the covered circle.)

qs.q: A solid consists of a cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 12 cm with a cone of the same radius and height 4 cm on top. Its volume is:
A toy is a cone of radius 2 cm and height 2 cm on a hemisphere of radius 2 cm. A right circular cylinder just encloses the toy. The difference between the volume of the cylinder and the toy is:

The radius of a sphere is increased by 25%. What is the increase per cent in surface area?
If the height of a circular cone is decreased by 10% and its radius is increased by 10%, then what will be the change in its volume?
The radius of a sphere is increased by 20%. The percentage increase in its volume is:
The radius of a sphere is doubled. Its volume becomes how many times the original?
Each edge of a cube is increased by 50%. The percentage increase in its surface area is:
The radius and height of a cylinder are each increased by 10%. The percentage increase in its volume is:
The radius of a cylinder is increased by 25%. By what percent must its height be reduced so that its volume remains the same?
qs.e: h × 1/(1.25)² = 16/25 ⇒ 36% less. (20% would keep only r × h fixed.)

qs.q: The radius of a cylinder is decreased by 50% and its height is increased by 50%. Its volume:
The radius of a cylinder open at both ends is decreased by 25% and its height is increased by 25%. Its curved surface area:
The volumes of two cubes are in the ratio 27 : 64. The ratio of their surface areas is:
A cone and a sphere have equal radii and equal volumes. The ratio of the cone's height to its radius is:
A cone and a hemisphere have equal bases and equal volumes. The ratio of their heights (cone : hemisphere) is:
qs.e: ⅓πr²h = ⅔πr³ ⇒ h = 2r; the hemisphere's height is r.

qs.q: A cylinder and a cone have equal radii, and their heights are in the ratio 2 : 3. The ratio of their volumes (cylinder : cone) is:
The radius of a sphere is decreased by 10%. Its volume decreases by:
The radius of a cone is doubled and its height is halved. Its volume increases by:
qs.e: r²h: 4 × ½ = 2 ⇒ +100%. (0% thinks doubling and halving cancel.)

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere increases by 21%. Its volume increases by:
The radius and height of a cylinder are each increased by 10%. The percentage increase in its total surface area is:
A cube of side 125 cm is painted red on all the faces and then cut into smaller cubes of sides 25 cm each. Find the number of smaller cubes having at least two faces painted.
Find the volume of the largest possible sphere circumscribed by a cube of edge 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
qs.e: Sphere inside the cube: r = 3.5; (4/3)(22/7)(42.875) = 179.67. SSC CHSL 2023 (3 Aug S2).

qs.q: What is the volume of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out of a cube of edge 12 cm (correct to two decimal places)?
A cube is painted on all faces and cut into 64 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have no face painted?
A painted cube is cut into 64 identical small cubes. How many of them have exactly one face painted?
A cube painted on all faces is cut into 125 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
A painted cube is cut into 216 equal small cubes. How many have at least one face painted?
A cube of edge 3 cm is cut into 1 cm cubes. The ratio of the total surface area of the small cubes to that of the original cube is:
The ratio of the volume of a cube to that of the largest sphere that fits inside it is:
The volume of the largest right circular cylinder that can be cut out of a cube of edge 14 cm is: (π = 22/7)
A sphere is inscribed in a cube, and the cube is inscribed in a bigger sphere. The ratio of the volume of the bigger sphere to that of the smaller sphere is:
qs.e: R : r = √3 : 1 ⇒ volumes (√3)³ = 3√3. (3 : 1 is the surface areas.)

qs.q: The largest cube that fits inside a sphere of radius 6√3 cm has edge:
qs.e: Space diagonal = diameter: a√3 = 12√3 ⇒ a = 12. (6√6 uses the face diagonal.)

qs.q: The surface area of the sphere that passes through all eight vertices of a cube of edge 4 cm is:
qs.e: R = 4√3/2 = 2√3; 4π(12) = 48π. (16π is the inscribed sphere; 32π uses the face diagonal.)

qs.q: A cuboid 24 cm × 18 cm × 12 cm is cut into the largest possible equal cubes with no waste. The number of cubes is:
The largest sphere that can be carved out of a cuboid 10 cm × 8 cm × 6 cm has volume:
qs.e: r = smallest edge/2 = 3: (4/3)π(27) = 36π. (500π/3 uses 10, 288π uses r = 6.)

qs.q: A cube of volume 216 cm³ is cut into 27 equal small cubes. The total surface area of all the small cubes is:
qs.e: Small edge 2: 27 × 6 × 4 = 648 (= 3 × 216). (432 is only the increase.)

qs.q: The ratio of the volume of the largest cone that can be cut from a cube to the volume of the cube is:
qs.e: ⅓π(a/2)²a = πa³/12 ⇒ π : 12. (π : 4 is the cylinder, π : 6 the sphere.)

qs.q: If tan θ = 3/4, then sin θ = ?

If sec θ = 13/5, then the value of (10 tan θ + 24 cosec θ)/(39 sin θ − 10 sec θ) is:
If cos θ = 5/13, then tan²θ + sec²θ = ?
qs.e: tan θ = 12/5, sec θ = 13/5 → 144/25 + 169/25 = 313/25. (1 is sec² − tan², not the sum.)

qs.q: If sin θ = 8/17 (θ acute), then tan θ + sec θ = ?
If tan θ = 1/√7, then (cosec²θ − sec²θ)/(cosec²θ + sec²θ) = ?
If sin A = 3/5 (A acute), then cosec A × sec A = ?
cosec θ × sin θ = ?
qs.e: cosec θ is the reciprocal of sin θ.

qs.q: If 3 cot A = 4, then (1 − tan²A)/(1 + tan²A) = ?
In △ABC, ∠B = 90°, AB = 24 cm and BC = 7 cm. sin A = ?
qs.e: AC = 25. For angle A the opposite side is BC = 7 → sin A = 7/25.

qs.q: If 5 tan θ = 4, then (5 sin θ − 3 cos θ)/(5 sin θ + 2 cos θ) = ?
qs.e: Divide by cos θ: (5 tan θ − 3)/(5 tan θ + 2) = (4 − 3)/(4 + 2) = 1/6.

qs.q: If sin θ = 5/13 (θ acute), then cot θ + cosec θ = ?
Which of these cannot be the value of sin θ for any angle θ?
qs.e: sin θ = P/H and P can never exceed H, so sin θ ≤ 1.

qs.q: cot θ · sec θ is equal to:
qs.e: (cos θ/sin θ)(1/cos θ) = 1/sin θ = cosec θ.

qs.q: If cos A = 4/5 (A acute), then cosec A − cot A = ?
qs.e: sin A = 3/5 → cosec A = 5/3, cot A = 4/3 → 1/3.

qs.q: For an acute angle θ, which ratio can be greater than 1?
qs.e: tan θ = P/B can be any positive value (e.g. tan 60° = √3); sin and cos stay below 1.

qs.q: The value of cosec 30° − cos 60° is:
qs.e: cosec 30° = 2, cos 60° = ½ → 3/2. SSC CGL 2023 (26 Jul S1).

qs.q: What is the value of 5√3 cos 60° tan 30° − 3 cos 0° + 3 cos²45° + 2 sin²60°?
If cos(40° + x) = sin 30°, then the value of x is:
The value of sin²30°·cos²45° + 2 tan²30° − sec²60° is:
What is the value of 100(sin 15° cos 15°)?
qs.e: ½ sin 30° = ¼ → 25. SSC CHSL 2021 (3 Jun 2022 S3).

qs.q: What is the value of tan 15°?
sin 18° · cos 36° = ?
tan 75° + cot 75° = ?
The value of sin 75° is:
(tan²45° + sec²60°·sin²30° + cos²90°·sin²60°)/(cosec²90° + cot 90°·sin 60°) = ?
(tan 60°·cosec 30° + tan 30°·sec 60°)/(sin²60° + 2 cot²45° − sec²30°) = ?
sin 60° cos 30° + cos 60° sin 30° = ?
4 sin²60° + 3 tan²30° − 8 sin 45° cos 45° = ?

If sec A + tan A = 3, then cos A is equal to:
qs.e: sec A − tan A = 1/3 → sec A = 5/3 → cos A = 3/5. SSC CGL 2023 (21 Jul S1).

qs.q: If sec θ + tan θ = 5, then find the value of tan θ.
If sec θ + tan θ = 3, then the value of sec θ is:
qs.e: sec θ − tan θ = 1/3 → 2 sec θ = 10/3. SSC CGL Tier 2 (18 Nov 2020).

qs.q: (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)/(1 − 2 sin²θ·cos²θ) = ?
qs.e: sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ, so the ratio is 1. SSC CGL 2023 (17 Jul S4).

qs.q: Simplify (1 + sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)/(cos²θ + sin⁴θ).
qs.e: Both reduce to multiples of (1 − sin²θ cos²θ); θ = 90° gives 2/1. SSC CGL 2023 (24 Jul S4).

qs.q: If sec θ + tan θ = p (p > 1), then (cosec θ + 1)/(cosec θ − 1) = ?
qs.e: (1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)² = p². SSC CGL Tier 2 (13 Sep 2019).

qs.q: If cosec θ + cot θ = 4, then cos θ = ?
qs.e: cosec θ − cot θ = 1/4 → cosec θ = 17/8, cot θ = 15/8 → cos θ = cot θ/cosec θ = 15/17.

qs.q: If sin θ + cos θ = 7/5, then sin θ·cos θ = ?
If sin θ + cos θ = 7/5, then (sin θ − cos θ)² = ?
sin⁶θ + cos⁶θ + 3 sin²θ·cos²θ = ?
qs.e: sin⁶ + cos⁶ = 1 − 3 sin²θ cos²θ, so the total is 1.

qs.q: tan²θ − sin²θ is equal to:
For acute θ, √((1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ)) = ?
qs.e: Multiply inside by (1 + sin θ): (1 + sin θ)/cos θ = sec θ + tan θ.

qs.q: sin²θ + 1/(1 + tan²θ) = ?
sin A(1 + tan A) + cos A(1 + cot A) = ?
qs.e: = (sin A + cos A)(tan A + cot A) = (sin A + cos A)/(sin A cos A) = sec A + cosec A.

qs.q: If tan θ + cot θ = 3, then tan²θ + cot²θ = ?
qs.e: (tan θ + cot θ)² − 2 tan θ cot θ = 9 − 2 = 7.

qs.q: If x = a sec θ and y = b tan θ, then x²/a² − y²/b² = ?
cos θ/(1 − sin θ) + cos θ/(1 + sin θ) = ?
qs.e: cos θ(2)/(1 − sin²θ) = 2 cos θ/cos²θ = 2 sec θ.

qs.q: If sec θ − cos θ = 14 and 14 sec θ = x, then x = ?
qs.e: sec θ − cos θ = sin²θ/cos θ = 14 → 14 sec θ = sin²θ/cos²θ = tan²θ.

qs.q: The value of cot 13° cot 27° cot 60° cot 63° cot 77° is:
qs.e: cot 13°·cot 77° = 1, cot 27°·cot 63° = 1, left cot 60° = 1/√3. SSC CHSL 2023 (2 Aug S2).

qs.q: If sin 3A = cos(30° − A), where A is acute, then 2 cosec A + tan²2A − cot²A = ?
(2 sin²38° sec²52° + cos 64° sin 26° + sin²64°)/(tan²23° + cot²23° − sec²67° − cosec²67°) = ?
qs.e: Numerator 2 + 1 = 3; denominator −1 − 1 = −2. SSC CGL Tier 2 (15 Nov 2020).

qs.q: [3(cot²47° − sec²43°) − 2(tan²23° − cosec²67°)] / [cosec²(68° + θ) − tan(θ + 61°) − tan²(22° − θ) + cot(29° − θ)] = ?
qs.e: Num: 3(−1) − 2(−1) = −1. Den: cosec²(68° + θ) − cot²(68° + θ) = 1 and cot(29° − θ) = tan(61° + θ) cancel → 1. SSC CGL Tier 2 (29 Jan 2022).

qs.q: The value of tan 1°·tan 2°·tan 3° … tan 89° is:
qs.e: Pairs (θ, 90° − θ) give tan θ·cot θ = 1; middle tan 45° = 1.

qs.q: sin²1° + sin²2° + sin²3° + … + sin²89° = ?
qs.e: 44 pairs of (sin² + cos²) = 44, plus sin²45° = ½ → 44½.

qs.q: cos 1° × cos 2° × cos 3° × … × cos 100° = ?
If tan 2A = cot(A − 18°), where 2A is acute, then A = ?
If sec 4A = cosec(A − 20°), where 4A is acute, then A = ?
If A + B = 90° and sin A = 3/5, then tan B = ?
sin 25° sec 65° + cos 25° cosec 65° = ?
cos 70°/sin 20° + cos 59°·cosec 31° − 8 sin²30° = ?
sin²20° + sin²70° + tan 30°·tan 60° = ?
tan 10° tan 15° tan 75° tan 80° = ?
If sin 2A = cos 3A and both angles are acute, then A = ?
sin²5° + sin²10° + sin²15° + … + sin²85° = ?
qs.e: 17 terms: 8 pairs (= 8) + sin²45° = ½ → 8½. (19/2 would include sin²90°.)

qs.q: If tan A·tan B = 1 (A, B acute), then sin(A + B) = ?
qs.e: tan A = cot B → A + B = 90° → sin 90° = 1.

qs.q: The value of 1/(cosec θ − cot θ) − 1/sin θ is equal to:
qs.e: 1/(cosec θ − cot θ) = cosec θ + cot θ → minus cosec θ leaves cot θ. SSC CGL 2024 (23 Sep S2).

qs.q: If cot θ = 4/3, then evaluate: sec θ(1 + cot²θ)(cosec²θ − cot²θ)/cosec³θ.
qs.e: = sec θ·cosec²θ/cosec³θ = tan θ = 3/4. SSC CGL 2024 (10 Sep S2).

qs.q: If tan x/sec x = 1/2 (x acute), then the value of (sin x + cos x)² is:
cot²θ − cosec²θ equals:
qs.e: cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1, so the reverse is −1. SSC CHSL 2023 (17 Aug S1).

qs.q: The value of (2 cos³θ − cos θ)/(sin θ − 2 sin³θ) is:
qs.e: cos θ(2cos²θ − 1)/[sin θ(1 − 2 sin²θ)] and 1 − 2 sin²θ = 2 cos²θ − 1 → cot θ. SSC CPO 2022 (10 Nov S1).

qs.q: (sec θ − cos θ)(cosec θ − sin θ)(tan θ + cot θ) = ?
(1 + tan θ + sec θ)(1 + cot θ − cosec θ) = ?
qs.e: Put θ = 45°: (2 + √2)(2 − √2) = 4 − 2 = 2. (Algebra gives the same for every θ.)

qs.q: cos A/(1 + tan A) − sin A/(1 + cot A) = ?
qs.e: = cos²A/(sin A + cos A) − sin²A/(sin A + cos A) = cos A − sin A.

qs.q: √(sec²θ + cosec²θ) = ?
qs.e: sec²θ + cosec²θ = 1/(sin²θ cos²θ) = (tan θ + cot θ)².

qs.q: cos θ/(1 + sin θ) = ?

qs.q: In the passive voice, the pronoun “we” after “by” becomes:
qs.e: Object form of we is us.
qs.tag: The rules: object, V3 and pronouns

qs.q: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. She invited us to the party.
o: We were invited to the party by her.
We was invited to the party by her.
Us were invited to the party by her.
We were invited to the party by she.
qs.e: Simple past; us → we (plural → were); she → by her.
qs.tag: The rules: object, V3 and pronouns

qs.q: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The teacher praised the students.
o: The students were praised by the teacher.
The students was praised by the teacher.
The students are praised by the teacher.
The teacher was praised by the students.
qs.e: Simple past; students is plural → were praised.
qs.tag: The rules: object, V3 and pronouns

qs.q: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He helps them.
qs.e: Simple present; them → they; he → him.
qs.tag: The rules: object, V3 and pronouns

qs.q: Which sentence has NO passive form?
qs.e: “have” meaning own/possess is a verb of state and is not made passive.
qs.tag: The rules: object, V3 and pronouns

qs.q: “She resembles her mother.” The passive voice of this sentence is:
o: Not possible; “resemble” is not used in the passive
Her mother is resembled by her.
Her mother was resembled by her.
Her mother is being resembled by her.
qs.e: Resemble is a state verb and has no passive.

qs.q: In “The boy kicked the ball”, which word becomes the subject in the passive?
qs.e: The object (the ball) becomes the subject.
qs.tag: The rules: object, V3 and pronouns
